newsitem.title: USA: Argentina to be stronger corn competitor-US group.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to be stronger corn competitor-US group.

text.p: Argentina will be a stronger competitor in the world corn market in the future, members of a U.S. Feed Grains Council tour said Tuesday from Colombia.

During a telephone news conference, five U.S. corn growers described steps in Argentina to boost output and reduce shipping costs. They also reported on growing demand in Colombia for U.S. corn for poultry, dairy and pork use.
Argentina was "going to be a competitor in the future, probably on a greater scale than at present," Vic Miller, an Iowa grower, told reporters, adding, "We can compete as well as they can."

Miller, Dick Works of Kansas and Raymond Schlabs of Texas said Argentina was expanding corn production and a project was under way to dredge part of the Paranon River to allow deeper-draft vessels to load at Rosario, 300 km northwest of Buenos Aires. Rail and grain storage capacity also was being expanded.

Theresa Schmalshof of Illinois and Gary Krug of Michigan said Colombia, now the largest South American market for U.S. corn with purchases of 1.4 million tonnes a year, could be a growing market. Poultry and pork producers want to expand production.
Schmalshof said some importers were concerned expansion of the Mercosur trade group would cut into U.S. corn sales.
A "substantial amount" of high-oil U.S. corn was being fed to Colombian poultry flocks, Krug said. Colombian interest in value-enhanced grain, such as high-oil corn "depends on price."
The five growers visited Argentina and Colombia as part of a council program to familiarize U.S. producers with export-market issues.
